ig_caption:
Depth First Search (DFS) Traversal on Real Street Maps ⚡ Wait—DFS doesn’t “search shortest”… it goes *deep first*.

On a real-street grid, we convert intersections → nodes and street segments → edges, then run DFS with a stack (LIFO). The traversal keeps moving forward along one path until it hits a dead end, then backtracks step-by-step—so the visited order reveals the DFS “spine” of the route.

Technical breakdown (quick):
• graph traversal = nodes(major intersections) + edges(street links)
• DFS uses recursion/stack → last-in, first-out exploration
• time complexity: O(V+E), space: O(V) for visited + call stack
• visual takeaway: DFS is great for reachability, cycle detection, and component discovery—NOT shortest paths (that’s BFS/Dijkstra)

Debate question: Would you prefer DFS to find a “path fast,” or BFS to find the “fewest intersections” on a map?
